notes: Live Atlassian MCP fetch is non-deterministic in eval subagents, so each prompt supplies the ticket as a file (treated as already-fetched) plus a small fixture codebase to verify claims against. The approval gate means autonomous runs are expected to stop at phase 5 (present-for-approval) without editing — phases 2-4 (intent, claim verification, plan reconciliation) are the differentiated value being graded.

evals.name: false-claim-premise
evals.prompt: You're picking up JIRA ticket PORTAL-481. The Atlassian fetch has already been done — the full ticket content is in /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-implement-workspace/fixtures/eval-1-false-claim/ticket.md (treat it as the fetched ticket; getJiraIssue is unavailable in this environment, so read the file instead). The working codebase is the single file /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-implement-workspace/fixtures/eval-1-false-claim/codebase/auth.js (treat this as src/auth.js). Pick up and action this ticket.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that input validation already exists in auth.js (validateLoginInput + the 400 short-circuit in login), classifies the ticket's 'no input validation at all' claim as FALSE with file:line evidence, identifies the false claim as load-bearing (the ticket's whole ask is to add validation that's already there), and stops to surface this to the user rather than implementing the proposed helper or editing auth.js.

assertions.text: Identifies that input validation already exists in auth.js, citing validateLoginInput and/or the 400 short-circuit with file:line evidence
Classifies the ticket's 'no input validation' claim as FALSE (not confirmed or partial)
Treats the false claim as load-bearing and stops/surfaces it rather than proceeding to implement
Does NOT edit auth.js or add a duplicate validateLoginInput function
Asks the user how to proceed (premise invalidated) instead of silently closing or silently building
Separates the ticket's goal from its codebase claims from its proposed solution

evals.name: flawed-proposed-solution
evals.prompt: You're picking up JIRA ticket CHK-1190. The Atlassian fetch has already been done — the full ticket content is in /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-implement-workspace/fixtures/eval-2-flawed-solution/ticket.md (treat it as the fetched ticket; getJiraIssue is unavailable, so read the file). The working codebase is the directory /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-implement-workspace/fixtures/eval-2-flawed-solution/codebase/ (orders.js as src/orders.js, schema.sql as the orders migration). Pick up and action this ticket.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the ticket's claims as true (no uniqueness constraint beyond PK in schema.sql; submitOrder inserts unconditionally in orders.js) with evidence. Designs its own plan before adopting the ticket's in-memory Set approach. Catches that an in-memory Set is unsafe given the service runs as 4 PM2 cluster workers (the Set isn't shared across processes and is lost on restart), and instead recommends a durable mechanism (DB unique constraint / idempotency key). Reconciliation keeps the author's dedup intent/signature idea but rejects in-memory storage, naming per-dimension winners. Stops at the approval gate before editing.

assertions.text: Verifies the 'no uniqueness constraint' and 'unconditional insert' claims as true/confirmed with file:line evidence
Designs an independent plan before adopting or endorsing the ticket's proposed in-memory Set
Identifies that the in-memory Set is unsafe under multi-process/cluster execution (4 PM2 workers) and/or lost on restart
Recommends a durable dedup mechanism (DB unique constraint or idempotency key) instead of the in-memory Set
Reconciliation names per-dimension winners and mines the proposed solution for its useful parts (dedup goal / signature concept) rather than discarding or rubber-stamping it
Stops at an approval gate before editing any file

evals.name: clean-no-proposed-solution
evals.prompt: You're picking up JIRA ticket INV-72. The Atlassian fetch has already been done — the full ticket content is in /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-implement-workspace/fixtures/eval-3-clean/ticket.md (treat it as the fetched ticket; getJiraIssue is unavailable, so read the file). The working codebase is the single file /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-implement-workspace/fixtures/eval-3-clean/codebase/currency.js (treat this as src/currency.js). Pick up and action this ticket.
evals.expected_output: Verifies both claims as confirmed with evidence (formatMoney uses toFixed(2) so always two decimals; SYMBOLS has no JPY entry). Does not manufacture any false positives. Produces a sound plan: add JPY with zero decimals and the ¥ symbol, preserve USD/EUR/GBP two-decimal behavior, and ideally notices that the ¥1,235 target needs thousands-separator grouping that toFixed doesn't provide (Intl.NumberFormat / toLocaleString). Recognizes there is no proposed solution and does not invent one. Stops at the approval gate before editing.

assertions.text: Verifies both claims (always two decimals via toFixed(2); no JPY symbol mapping) as confirmed with file:line evidence
Does NOT manufacture false positives — no accurate claim is wrongly marked false
Plan adds JPY support with zero decimal places and the ¥ symbol
Plan preserves existing USD/EUR/GBP two-decimal formatting
Notices the ¥1,235 target requires thousands-separator grouping that toFixed does not produce
Recognizes there is no proposed solution and does not invent a comparison; stops at an approval gate before editing
